thread:
Noah Kim: kicking off Solace POC thread. scope: contract/statement search + two tool calls (create_invoice, update_payment_status). Sales asked for a brief SOW, explicit acceptance criteria, model recommendations for long-form docs, and an estimated committed pricing for ~10k q/day. Demo target: 9 business days.

Elena V.: proposed acceptance criteria: precision@5 >= 0.80 on customer-labeled set, E2E tool-call success >= 95% (schema + observed side-effect verification), search-path p95 < 500ms under POC load, and automated PII redaction enabled with low false negatives.

Marcus Li: model-fit thought: documents include multi-section contracts and statements; suggest testing a 64k-context family for an initial quality baseline (to capture whole-doc context). If 64k cost/latency is prohibitive, fall back to 32k then 16k plus chunking heuristics. Two-stage retrieval: sparse lexical filter -> dense embeddings ANN -> learned cross-encoder reranker (small quantized model) -> generator for tool payload. Unique note: try sparse+dense hybrid to trim candidates before expensive rerank.

Sofia Grant: timeline proposal: Days 0-2 connectors + canonical prompt collection (need 50 labeled prompts from Solace), Days 3-5 embedding + index build + sparse hybrid tuning, Days 6-7 reranker tuning & prompt templates, Day8 tool integration + E2E smoke, Day9 demo + acceptance. Engineering requests sample doc corpus by Day1 to validate context decisions.

Noah Kim: acceptance wording for SOW: precision@5 >= 0.80 on Solace test set OR equivalent human-validated results for ambiguous queries, avg token cost per search+gen <= $0.0035 (hosted estimate) or committed reserved rate, tool-call success >= 95% with schema validation, and no outstanding security findings. Add explicit rollback to 32k/16k + chunking if 64k tests exceed cost/latency caps.

Elena V.: Solace security asks: SAML SSO + SCIM, BYOK via customer KMS, audit log retention 12 months, SOC2 report, and completed security questionnaire. They'll send back the questionnaire and SSO test creds within 48 hours. Add breach notification SLA and incident response contact in SOW.

Marcus Li: embeddings sizing: Solace estimates ~300k documents, average 3.5KB -> ~1.05B tokens. Start with 768-d embeddings for speed; if semantic recall lags, try 1024-d. Index storage estimate ~40-60GB compressed depending on HNSW paramization. Recommend nightly incremental refresh + webhook-triggered immediate embedding for new high-priority docs.

Sofia Grant: pricing ask: finance wants usage profile. Example calc: 10k q/day -> ~300k q/mo. Provide two options: hosted metered (per-query + per-token) and reserved monthly commit with a lower unit price + SLA. I'll open a finance request.

Noah Kim: engineering checklist: 1) validate 64k latency & 95th pct on a sampled subset, 2) instrument token-level cost and route breakdown, 3) implement sparse+dense pipeline flags and rerank A/B toggles, 4) add schema validation and replay tests for tool side-effects, 5) PII redaction checks.

Marcus Li: sample curl for semsearch + hybrid rerank (POC engineer):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/semsearch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"What are the steps to dispute an invoice?","top_k":200,"sparse_filter":true,"hybrid":true,"rerank":true,"model":"rwd-64k-search"}'
```

Elena V.: ops question: embedding refresh cadence? Solace requires same-day for invoices but is ok with nightly for contracts. We'll propose nightly by default plus webhook-forced refresh for invoices. Who owns refresh scheduling in SOW? Ops or customer? Need explicit owner.

InfraBot: POCTICKET-SOLACE-2125209999 created, infra ticket INF-9120 opened, service account provisioned, KMS onboarding pending customer's key-sharing approval.

Noah Kim: blockers to flag on the call: 1) security questionnaire & SSO creds, 2) finance committed pricing approval, 3) sampled doc corpus to validate 64k latency, 4) KMS key handshake for BYOK.

Sofia Grant: I'll draft the SOW tonight: timeline, acceptance criteria, rollback plan (64k -> 32k/16k + chunking), prompt-eval plan (50 labeled prompts across intents), instrumentation to capture precision@1/5, recall@10, avg tokens/query, token cost, p95 latency, and tool-call success.

Marcus Li: extra POC note: run a small experiment to compare full-doc 64k vs chunked 32k+context-window fusion; collect quality delta vs token-cost to inform final recommendation.

Noah Kim: great. next sync Wed 10am PT. Please upload the prompt set and sample corpus before EOD tomorrow. Thanks all. :rocket:
